=== ACCESS RULES (STRICT) ===
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, commit, push, or post anything to GitHub.
- DO NOT check out any branch. The working tree holds unrelated uncommitted work.
- The PR is fetched as the local ref `pr/61`. Read files with `git show pr/61:<path>`.
- Base (merge-base with develop) is `8362b3c`. Read base files with `git show 8362b3c:<path>`.
- Diff with `git diff 8362b3c pr/61 [-- <path>]`.
- DO NOT re-run any gate (no npm test/lint/build/tsc/playwright). Gates were already measured; the numbers are below. Your entire budget goes to what gates CANNOT see.

=== THE PR ===
#61 "SFCC-751: BrowserStack/Zephyr Scale QA automation pipeline", author TimLavelleACC,
`feature/browserstack-ci-automation` -> `develop`. 42 files, +2886/-266, 20 commits.
Head 74e2b82. CodeRabbit approved after several CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds; no human review yet.

=== JIRA TICKET SFCC-751 — VERBATIM, AS WRITTEN ===
Title: SFCC-751: QA Pipeline — Playwright spec generation, BrowserStack execution, and Zephyr Scale result sync

Overview
Implement the end-to-end QA pipeline that closes the loop between Zephyr Scale test cases and BrowserStack Automate execution results. This story covers three discrete deliverables that must be in place for the AI-assisted QA methodology to function as designed.

Background
Zephyr test case SFCC-T150 has been created and linked to SFCC-420. The pipeline requires:
- A Playwright spec tagged with the Zephyr test case key so BrowserStack knows what it is executing
- A GitHub Actions workflow that fetches BrowserStack results and posts execution records back to Zephyr Scale via the EU regional API
- A validated end-to-end run confirming the full chain works

Deliverables
Deliverable 1 — Playwright spec (SFCC-T150)
- Generate e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/SFCC-420-global-e-job-site-assignments.p1.spec.ts
- Spec must be tagged with Zephyr test case key SFCC-T150
- Scenarios must cover all 6 BDD scenarios in SFCC-T150
- Selectors via POM only — no inline selectors
- Tagged @SFCC-420 @global-e @integration @p1

Deliverable 2 — GitHub Actions sync script
- New workflow: .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml
- Triggers on completion of BrowserStack Automate run in CI
- Fetches BrowserStack session results via BrowserStack REST API
- Maps BrowserStack pass/fail to Zephyr test case key via spec tag
- Posts execution record to Zephyr Scale EU endpoint: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions
- Attaches BrowserStack session URL and HAR to Zephyr execution record
- Zephyr API token stored as GitHub Actions secret: ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN
- BrowserStack credentials stored as: BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME, BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY

Deliverable 3 — End-to-end validation
- Trigger a BrowserStack run against the new spec
- Confirm execution record appears in Zephyr under SFCC-T150
- Confirm BrowserStack session URL is attached to the Zephyr execution record
- Document any manual steps required for ongoing operation

Acceptance Criteria
- Given a merged Playwright spec tagged with a Zephyr test case key, when BrowserStack Automate completes a run in CI, then an execution record is created in Zephyr Scale under the correct test case with pass/fail status and BrowserStack session URL attached
- Given the sync script runs, when it calls the Zephyr API, then it uses the EU regional endpoint https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 and not the US default
- Given a BrowserStack run fails, when the sync script posts to Zephyr, then the execution record status is Failed and the BrowserStack session URL for debugging is included
- Given the pipeline runs end-to-end, when reviewed in Zephyr Scale, then SFCC-T150 shows an execution record linked to the BrowserStack run with correct status

Design/Technical Notes
- Zephyr Scale instance is on EU/DE regional API: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2
- Do NOT use the US default endpoint https://api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 — returns unknown token errors
- BrowserStack Automate REST API
- Zephyr Scale test executions API: POST /testexecutions with testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment
- The .browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically
- Playwright spec naming convention: {JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts
=== END VERBATIM TICKET ===

=== ALREADY-MEASURED GATE RESULTS (do not re-run; do not treat as evidence of correctness) ===
The PR touches ZERO files under `overrides/`. Nearly every gate here is scoped to `overrides/`:
- `npm run lint` scope `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` -> covers 0/42 PR files; not run in qa.yml
- `npm run audit:tokens` scope overrides components/theme -> 0/42; not in CI; exits 1 at a HEALTHY baseline (14 known pre-existing violations)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` tsconfig include ['overrides/**/*','vitest.config.ts','vitest.setup.ts'] -> covers 1/42 (vitest.config.ts only)
- Vitest include ['overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)'], passWithNoTests:true -> 0/42 changed files; CI job PASSED (1m46s) only because detect-changes watches vitest.config.*
- Storybook a11y/interaction -> 0/42 changed; PASSED (2m57s) only because package.json/lock changed
- Playwright E2E (localhost): SKIPPING. Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack): SKIPPING.
- Deploy Preview PASSED. File Tier & Squad Boundary Check PASSED.
Also known: `npm run test:max-file-size` exits 1 on a healthy tree (main.js ~352kB vs 180kB budget, vendor.js ~2MB vs 550kB) and is not in CI. `npm run test:contracts` is a permanent `echo && exit 0` stub.
A SKIPPED required check counts as PASSING on the merge button in this repo.
=> Do NOT read any of these non-zero exits or green checks as evidence about this PR.

=== RUBRIC SOURCE ===
Read house rules at BASE `8362b3c`, not head — this PR edits `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/testing.md`, two of the files it would be judged against.

=== ALREADY SETTLED BY THE LEAD — do not re-litigate, do not spend budget here ===
The `.browserstack.yml` -> `browserstack.yml` rename did NOT drop the file's Tier 1 status. At head, `frozenFiles.md:114` re-lists the un-dotted path with rationale and `CODEOWNERS:60` routes it to tier-1-approvers. (Still open, and fair game: `protected-file-guard.yml` has no browserstack entry at base OR head.)

=== YOUR ANGLE: R1 — CORRECTNESS & REGRESSION (CI control flow) ===
Does this pipeline actually do what the ticket says? What breaks that the diff does not obviously touch?

Trace every execution path through:
- .github/workflows/qa.yml
- .github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml
- scripts/computeBuildName.mjs (new), scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs (new, 359 lines)
- browserstack.yml (new, un-dotted), playwright.config.js
- the two new specs under e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/ and the page objects in e2e/support/pages/

Specific targets (not exhaustive — find what I have not listed):
1. Enumerate EVERY route by which a job reports green having executed ZERO tests.
2. The `e2e_scope=homepage` allow-list logic in detect-changes vs THIS PR's own 42-file set. Which value does it produce, and why?
3. `--grep` zero-match: exit 0 or 1? Prove it, don't assume.
4. `computeBuildName.mjs`'s `unknown-{key}` fallback -> does the downstream build-name lookup in zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs then silently find nothing?
5. `deploy-preview.yml` fires on every `feature/**` push — does it contend for a shared MRT target with other developers' branches? What is the concurrency/target-naming scheme?
6. Trace call sites of anything modified. What existing behaviour regresses?

**SPECIAL ASSIGNMENT — ATTACK THIS PREMISE BY NAME.** Everyone in the chain (author, CodeRabbit's approval, the green checkmarks) has proceeded as if THIS PIPELINE HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED TO WORK. Attack that directly. What evidence exists that any part of this chain has executed successfully even once, end to end or in part? Report a result, not a restatement.

=== CONSTRAINTS ON YOUR OUTPUT (all mandatory) ===
- FALSIFY, do not confirm. Try to break each claim the PR makes about itself, including claims made in its own source-code comments.
- Cite `file:line` for every finding.
- Label each finding CONFIRMED (you reproduced//proved it) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned but unproven).
- Severity: BLOCKER, DEFECT, or NOTE.
- When a count moves, prove WHICH items moved, not just how many. Enumerate identity where the set is small enough.
- For any check whose pass you rely on, try to make it pass WRONGLY — construct a decoy case that should fail and reason through whether it would. A check never made to fail has not been shown capable of failing.
- Any "X exists nowhere" claim MUST state its search scope in the same sentence (e.g. "no reference to FOO in .github/workflows/ or scripts/ at pr/61").
- Separate what the author changed from what was already there. Pre-existing issues are NOTEs unless the PR's own premise makes them defects.
- MANDATORY CLOSING SECTION titled "What I could not verify": name what you could not reach and why. If you think the space is covered, show the search that establishes it. An empty section with no reasoning is a failed brief.

Be concrete and concise. No code dumps beyond the minimum needed to prove a point.

   196	      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
   197	      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to

   199	      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.
   200	      #
   201	      # Diffs against the previous push (github.event.before, only present on
   202	      # "synchronize"), not the base branch — same per-push reasoning as
   203	      # since_last_remote_commit on "Get changed files" above. Without this,
   204	      # a real dependency change on an earlier commit in the PR would leave
   205	      # runtime_changed=true (and so e2e/vitest forced on) for every later
   206	      # push, even a docs-only one, since it ORs into both outputs below.
   207	      # Falls back to the base branch on "opened"/"reopened", where there's
   208	      # no meaningful previous-push SHA yet.

   210	        id: deps
   211	        run: |
   212	          if [[ "${{ github.event.action }}" == "synchronize" ]]; then
   213	            BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.before }}"
   214	            git fetch origin "$BASE_SHA" --depth=1
   215	          else
   216	            git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
   217	            BASE_SHA="origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
   218	          fi
   219	          BASE_DEPS=$(git show "$BASE_SHA:package.json" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).dependencies||{})))")

   222	            echo "runtime_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   223	          else
   224	            echo "runtime_changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   225	          fi
   226	
   227	      - name: Persist e2e relevance for e2e-browserstack-preview.yml
   228	        env:
   229	          E2E_RELEVANT: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
   230	        run: printf '{"e2e":"%s"}\n' "$E2E_RELEVANT" > "$E2E_RELEVANT_OUT"
   231	
   232	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   233	        with:
   234	          name: e2e-scope
   235	          path: ${{ env.E2E_RELEVANT_OUT }}
   236	          retention-days: 1
   237	
   238	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   239	  # Unit tests — runs on every PR to develop and release/**

1	name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
     2	
     3	# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
     4	# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
     5	# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
     6	# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
     7	# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
     8	# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
     9	# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
    10	# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
    11	# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
    12	# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
    13	#

    15	# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
    16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
    17	#
    18	# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
    19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
    20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
    21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
    22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.

    24	  workflow_run:
    25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
    26	    types: [completed]
    27	
    28	permissions:
    29	  contents: read
    30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
    31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch
    32	
    33	jobs:
    34	  e2e-browserstack:
    35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    37	    # Only a fully cancelled Deploy Preview run has nothing to fall back to
    38	    # (no hostname artifact could ever exist). Any other conclusion still
    39	    # gets a shot at the static test-tier fallback below — same graceful-
    40	    # degradation the old polling design had.
    41	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    42	    timeout-minutes: 25
    43	    environment: test # for vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME (fallback target) and the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
    44	    steps:
    45	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
    46	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
    47	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
    48	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
    49	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
    50	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
    51	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
    52	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
    53	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
    54	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
    55	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
    56	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    57	        with:
    58	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
    59	
    60	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    61	        with:
    62	          node-version: '24'
    63	          cache: 'npm'
    64	
    65	      - name: Install dependencies
    66	        run: npm install --include=dev
    67	
    68	      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
    69	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
    70	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.
    71	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
    72	        id: pr
    73	        env:
    74	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    75	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
    76	        run: |
    77	          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
    78	            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')
    79	          if [[ -z "$PR_JSON" ]]; then
    80	            echo "No open PR found for branch $BRANCH -- nothing to test."
    81	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    82	            exit 0
    83	          fi
    84	          BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')
    85	          if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
    86	            # deploy-preview.yml only triggers on feature/**, fix/** pushes,
    87	            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
    88	            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
    89	            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
    90	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    91	            exit 0
    92	          fi
    93	          echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    94	          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    95	          # Title/body go to files, not GITHUB_OUTPUT -- both are
    96	          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
    97	          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.
    98	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.title' > pr-title.txt
    99	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""' > pr-body.txt
   100	
   101	      # Same regex/signal as qa.yml's detect-changes "Detect Jira story
   102	      # keys" step. Duplicated rather than shared across workflows -- small
   103	      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
   104	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story
   105	      # BrowserStack/Zephyr run to, so skip (mirrors the old "job doesn't
   106	      # run at all" behaviour, not a fallback-to-full).
   107	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
   108	        id: jira
   109	        if: steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'
   110	        env:
   111	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
   112	        run: |
   113	          KEYS=$( { cat pr-title.txt pr-body.txt; printf '%s\n' "$BRANCH"; } \
   114	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
   115	          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   116	
   117	      # Single-shot lookup of the QA run for this same commit -- no loop.
   118	      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy
   119	      # Preview takes several minutes minimum, so by the time this job
   120	      # starts, that artifact is essentially guaranteed to already exist.
   121	      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open
   122	      # (assume e2e-relevant) rather than adding a retry loop to chase an
   123	      # optimisation -- worst case this runs BrowserStack once when
   124	      # detect-changes would have skipped it, not a correctness problem.
   125	      - name: Look up matching QA run
   126	        id: qa-run
   127	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   128	        env:
   129	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
   130	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
   131	        run: |
   132	          RUN_ID=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/qa.yml/runs?head_sha=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
   133	          echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   134	
   135	      - name: Download e2e-relevance artifact
   136	        id: download-e2e-scope
   137	        if: steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''
   138	        continue-on-error: true
   139	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   140	        with:
   141	          name: e2e-scope
   142	          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
   143	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   144	
   145	      - name: Check e2e relevance
   146	        id: relevance
   147	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   148	        run: |
   149	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then
   150	            echo "Nothing e2e-relevant changed on this commit (per qa.yml's detect-changes) -- skipping BrowserStack."
   151	            echo "relevant=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   152	          else
   153	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   154	          fi
   155	
   156	      - name: Compute build name
   157	        id: build-name
   158	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   159	        run: |
   160	          PRIMARY_KEY=$(echo "${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}" | awk '{print $1}')
   161	          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
   162	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   163	        env:
   164	          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
   165	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   166	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}
   167	
   168	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
   169	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.
   170	      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
   171	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   172	        env:
   173	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   174	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt
   175	
   176	      - name: Upload build name artifact
   177	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   178	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   179	        with:
   180	          name: browserstack-build-name
   181	          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
   182	          retention-days: 7
   183	
   184	      # Deploy Preview persists this as an artifact on its own run only
   185	      # after a successful build+push (see that workflow's own comment) --
   186	      # a missing artifact here means either that run didn't reach that
   187	      # step, or it failed outright. Either way, fall back to the static
   188	      # test-tier target instead of failing this job, same as the old
   189	      # polling design did.
   190	      - name: Download preview hostname artifact
   191	        id: download-preview-hostname
   192	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   193	        continue-on-error: true
   194	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   195	        with:
   196	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
   197	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
   198	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   199	
   200	      - name: Resolve BrowserStack test target
   201	        id: resolve-target
   202	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   203	        run: |
   204	          if [[ -f preview-hostname.txt ]]; then
   205	            HOSTNAME=$(cat preview-hostname.txt)
   206	            echo "Testing this PR's own MRT preview: https://$HOSTNAME"
   207	            echo "retail_app_home=https://$HOSTNAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   208	          else
   209	            echo "No PR-specific preview available for this run -- falling back to the static test-tier RETAIL_APP_HOME."
   210	            echo "retail_app_home=${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   211	          fi
   212	
   213	      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
   214	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   215	        run: |
   216	          GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
   217	          npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"
   218	        env:
   219	          KEYS: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
   220	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
   221	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
   222	          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   223	          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ steps.resolve-target.outputs.retail_app_home }}
   224	          # Sent regardless of which target was resolved above. The `test`
   225	          # tier is access-gated (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-25)
   226	          # -- without this header every request is rejected before the
   227	          # page can load. Whether the PR's own MRT preview target also
   228	          # needs it is unconfirmed, but sending an extra header a target
   229	          # doesn't require is harmless. See BasePage.js's
   230	          # applyExtraHeaders() and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.
   231	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME }}
   232	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
   233	          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
   234	          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
   235	          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   236	          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   237	          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   238	          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   239	          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
   240	          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs

    29	    # lookup) may still have a real BrowserStack build worth syncing. The

    40	      # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25). No ref: means the
    41	      # default branch, which is also the only ref GitHub ever evaluates a
    42	      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
    43	      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself
    44	      # anyway (see .claude/rules/testing.md), so this costs nothing.

    46	
    47	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

    49	          node-version: '24'

    51	      # Must use the identical build name the triggering run's
    52	      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks

Refusing to fall back to the run number, which could silently miss a real BrowserStack build. Investigate the artifact upload step in the triggering workflow."

1	# browserstack.yml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
     2	# NOTE: named without a leading dot deliberately — browserstack-node-sdk
     3	# searches upward from cwd for exactly `browserstack.yml`; a `.browserstack.yml`
     4	# (this file's name until 2026-08-25) is never found, so every SDK-driven run
     5	# fails at config resolution before any test executes. Confirmed via
     6	# BrowserStack's own docs, and via a real CI failure on PR #61.
     7	# BrowserStack Playwright SDK configuration for cross-browser regression
     8	# Docs: https://www.browserstack.com/docs/automate/playwright/sdk-node
     9	
    10	userName: ${BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}
    11	accessKey: ${BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}
    12	
    13	# Top-level buildName/projectName govern the classic Automate dashboard's
    14	# build grouping — a different product from Test Observability below, which
    15	# has its own separate projectName/buildName under testObservabilityOptions.
    16	# Without this, Automate showed every run as "Untitled Build Run #N" even
    17	# though testObservabilityOptions.buildName was set correctly (confirmed
    18	# 2026-08-25). Keep both blocks' values in sync.
    19	buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"
    20	projectName: "Zim Project"
    21	
    22	framework: playwright
    23	
    24	# Zimmermann tests only
    25	testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm
    26	
    27	# `platforms:` (with browserName/browserVersion/os/osVersion), not the
    28	# classic Automate/Selenium `browsers:` key (browser/browser_version/
    29	# os/os_version) — the Playwright Node SDK only recognises the former.
    30	# `browsers:` is silently ignored: the SDK finds zero configured
    31	# platforms and every test falls through to a genuine local Playwright
    32	# launch instead of one on BrowserStack's cloud, which fails outright
    33	# in CI since no local browser binaries are installed there (that's
    34	# the SDK's job, remotely) — confirmed against the SDK's own installed
    35	# source (modifyPlaywrightConf.js only ever reads a `platforms` key)
    36	# and BrowserStack's current docs, after every desktop/mobile spec
    37	# failed this exact way on PR #61, 2026-08-25. Safari has no Playwright
    38	# driver of its own — `playwright-webkit` is BrowserStack's mapping for
    39	# testing WebKit-engine (Safari-equivalent) behaviour, same reasoning
    40	# for `playwright-firefox`. `chrome`/`edge` run for real since Playwright
    41	# drives them directly via CDP.
    42	#
    43	# This account's plan allows exactly ONE concurrent BrowserStack session
    44	# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26 — not the account's queue
    45	# ceiling this time, its actual `team_parallel_sessions_max_allowed`).
    46	# Every platform below therefore runs strictly sequentially — platform
    47	# count is a direct multiplier on wall-clock time and cost, with zero
    48	# parallelism benefit from adding more. That ruled out a broad "current
    49	# device − 2 generations" matrix across iPhone/Samsung/Pixel (would have
    50	# been 9 real-mobile platforms alone): on a 1-session plan, what a real
    51	# device buys you is OS/engine-version coverage, not device-generation
    52	# depth — an iPhone 15 and an iPhone 17 on the same iOS build render
    53	# near-identically, so one current device per platform we can't get any
    54	# other way beats three generations of one we can. Six platforms total:
    55	# three real devices (the coverage nothing else in this pipeline can
    56	# provide) plus the three desktop engines already established. Edge and
    57	# a second desktop Chrome OS were cut entirely — same Chromium engine as
    58	# the real Android devices below, lowest marginal value under a strict
    59	# 1-session budget.

    61	  # AU / US primary desktop browser
    62	  - os: OS X
    63	    osVersion: Sonoma
    64	    browserName: chrome
    65	    browserVersion: latest
    66	
    67	  # AU / US / HK significant Safari share (Apple-heavy luxury market) —
    68	  # desktop WebKit signal, distinct from the real iOS Safari device below
    69	  # (different rendering path: desktop vs. mobile Safari).
    70	  - os: OS X
    71	    osVersion: Sonoma
    72	    browserName: playwright-webkit
    73	    browserVersion: latest
    74	
    75	  # UK / EU / ME — the other non-Chromium desktop engine.
    76	  - os: Windows
    77	    osVersion: 11
    78	    browserName: playwright-firefox
    79	    browserVersion: latest
    80	
    81	  # Real iOS device, real Safari — not Playwright's desktop WebKit build
    82	  # (the entry above), which is a genuine engine but not the same
    83	  # rendering path as Mobile Safari (different scrolling, fixed-position,
    84	  # and viewport behaviour). BrowserStack added real-device Playwright
    85	  # Safari support industry-first, June 2025 — confirmed current via
    86	  # browserstack.com/guide/playwright-ios-automation and BrowserStack's
    87	  # own docs (2026-08-26). Current model, iPhone 17, on its ship OS,
    88	  # iOS 26 (confirmed live via web search, not training data — iPhone 17
    89	  # launched Sept 2025 with iOS 26 pre-installed). deviceName + osVersion
    90	  # + browserName: safari + realMobile: true is BrowserStack's documented
    91	  # real-device shape (no `os:` field, matching the Android entries'

    93	  # device catalogue (local `.env` BrowserStack creds are blank, so this

    99

   101	  # meaningfully different rendering environment from stock Android.
   102	  # Current model, Galaxy S26, on its ship OS: Android 16 / One UI 8.5
   103	  # (confirmed live via web search, 2026-08-26). Not yet live-verified
   104	  # against the device catalogue, same caveat as above.

   107	    browserName: chrome
   108	    realMobile: true
   109	
   110	  # Real Android device, Pixel — stock Android reference device, the

     2	 * Hand-maintained fixture-key -> URL-prefix map for E2E site-routing tests.
     3	 *
     4	 * site.js (SITE_CONFIGS) does not carry URL-prefix data — it only tracks
     5	 * siteId/locale/currency, derived from live SFCC data via
     6	 * `npm run sync:regional-config`. The URL prefix ('urlSlug') is a routing
     7	 * concept owned by overrides/app/config/countries.ts, keyed by the slug
     8	 * itself rather than this fixture's camelCase keys — this file bridges that
     9	 * gap without hand-editing the auto-generated site fixture.
    10	 *
    11	 * Keep in sync with overrides/app/config/countries.ts's COUNTRIES export.
    12	 * Verified directly against the live dev environment (2026-08-25): the

    14	 * `?site=usIntl` silently falls back to `us`, not an error) — only a direct
    15	 * path prefix (e.g. `/en-ca/`) reliably selects the intended site. These
    16	 * urlPrefix values are for path-prefix navigation, not the `?site=` param.
    17	 */
    18	module.exports = {
    19	  au: { urlPrefix: '' },
    20	  us: { urlPrefix: '/us' },

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+#    not the whole suite. `vitest related` walks the module graph from the
+#    given files and runs whatever test files transitively depend on them

+

+    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — a related Vitest test failed."
+    echo "      Fix the failure above, then re-stage and commit again."
+    echo ""
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+
 exit 0

diff --git a/.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml b/.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml
index fa28857..d29b6de 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml
@@ -14,34 +14,72 @@ on:
 
 jobs:
   # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-  # JOB 1 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 1 files touched.
-  # NOT a required status check (see AGENTS.md > Tier 1 Approval for why).
-  # The actual hard block is CODEOWNERS + require_code_owner_reviews on
-  # branch protection, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
-  # involvement. This job exists to post the loud, informative warning and
-  # owner-contact-map — useful context, not the gate itself.
-  #
-  # History: this used to be a required check with a second job
-  # (tier1-guard-recheck) that re-evaluated it on every review submission
-  # via the Checks API, so it could flip from fail to pass without a new
-  # commit. That approach stopped working once GitHub locked down check-run
-  # updates to same-run-only in Feb 2025 (see
-  # https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-12-notice-of-upcoming-deprecations-and-breaking-changes-for-github-actions/#changes-to-check-run-status-modification) —
-  # a different workflow run can no longer flip another run's check
-  # conclusion. Since a single pull_request-triggered run can't wait around
-  # for a future review, and re-running the whole job on review events just
-  # creates a second, stale-vs-fresh check-run record under the same name
-  # (which GitHub does NOT treat the newer one as superseding for
-  # merge-blocking purposes), there's no way to make this job itself both
-  # required and reliably self-updating. CODEOWNERS already does this
-  # correctly and natively, so that's the real gate.
+  # JOB 1 — Hard block: PR targeting wrong branch.
+  # Kept as its OWN job, unmerged with the informational checks below —
+  # "🔴 Branch Target Check" is a REQUIRED status check on develop, main,
+  # and release/** branch protection (confirmed live via the Branch
+  # Protection API, 2026-08-25). Folding it into a combined job would
+  # rename what GitHub sees as reporting that check, silently breaking
+  # required-status-check enforcement (merges would block forever until
+  # someone updated the branch protection settings to the new name) —
+  # not worth the minutes saving. The other three checks below are not
+  # required by any branch protection rule (confirmed the same way),
+  # so those are safe to combine into one job.
   # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-  tier1-guard:
-    name: "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"
+  branch-target-guard:
+    name: '🔴 Branch Target Check'
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     permissions:
       contents: read
-      pull-requests: read
+    steps:
+      - name: Block direct PRs to main from feature branches
+        run: |
+          BASE="${{ github.base_ref }}"
+          HEAD="${{ github.head_ref }}"
+
+          echo "Base branch: $BASE"
+          echo "Head branch: $HEAD"
+
+          # Feature branches must not go directly to main
+          if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
+            echo ""
+            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
+            echo "🔴 INVALID BRANCH TARGET"

1	    # Without this, a genuinely unreachable SFCC dev org (or any other
     2	    # unbounded hang outside Playwright's own per-test timeout/retry
     3	    # budget) rides GitHub's default 6-hour job ceiling instead of failing
     4	    # fast with a clear signal. 15 is measured, not padded: setup (checkout
     5	    # -> deps -> browsers -> dev server) took ~1m30s and a real full-retry
     6	    # SFCC-dev-org-down failure took 12m13s on the Playwright step alone

     9	    timeout-minutes: 15
    10	    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
    11	    # Re-enabled 2026-07-16 on bugfix/ci-e2e-test to actively debug the
    12	    # homepage smoke test failure — now confirmed fixed (see
    13	    # .docs/memory/projectState.md) with better diagnostics: an HTML report
    14	    # now gets generated (playwright.config.js), while Playwright retains
    15	    # its default two retries for each CI iteration.
    16	    # unit-tests may now report "skipped" rather than "success" (see
    17	    # detect-changes above) — GitHub's implicit success() over all `needs`
    18	    # would otherwise treat a skipped unit-tests as blocking this job too.
    19	    # !cancelled() bypasses that default so we can explicitly allow skipped
    20	    # — unlike always(), it still stops this job from continuing on a
    21	    # cancelled workflow run (e.g. superseded by a newer push), instead of
    22	    # burning a 15-minute runner slot on a run nobody's waiting on.
    23	    if: |
    24	      !cancelled() &&
    25	      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
    26	      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope != 'skip' &&
    27	      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')

    29	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    30	
    31	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    32	        with:
    33	          node-version: '24'
    34	          cache: 'npm'
    35	
    36	      - name: Install dependencies
    37	        run: npm install --include=dev
    38	
    39	      - name: Install Playwright browsers
    40	        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
    41	
    42	      - name: Start dev server
    43	        # Output wasn't captured anywhere before — a backgrounded process's
    44	        # stdout/stderr doesn't show up in the step's own log. Redirecting to
    45	        # a file (uploaded below, always) is the only way to see an SSR
    46	        # crash/error server-side instead of just the client-visible symptom
    47	        # (a non-200 response, or a page that never finishes rendering).
    48	        run: npm start > dev-server.log 2>&1 &
    49	        env:
    50	          # DEPLOY_TARGET (not ENVIRONMENT_NAME) is what
    51	          # @salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime's getConfig() reads to pick
    52	          # config/<target>.js — must be a real process env var before

    55	          DEPLOY_TARGET: dev

    61	          PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
    62	          COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID }}
    63	          COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID }}
    64	          COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE }}
    65	          COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID }}
    66	
    67	      - name: Wait for dev server

+`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
+what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
+target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
+below for why):
+
+- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
+  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
+  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
+- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
+  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
+  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).
+
+Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
+`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.
+
+**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
+integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
+Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
+flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
+results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
+(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
+the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
+per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
+result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
+Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
+story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
+confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
+attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
+evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
+execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.
+
+**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
+GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
+**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
+GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
+what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
+PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
+itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
+`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
+`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
+`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
+`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
+triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
+`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
+directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
+the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
+has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
+carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
+`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
+(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.
+
+**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
+derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
+scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
+`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
+grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
+the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
+`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
+Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
+that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
+recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
+workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
+`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a

+this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
+independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
+guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
+documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
+`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that

+fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
+correctly, 2026-08-25).

+Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
+Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
+mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
+to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
+result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11

+`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
+does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

+`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
+project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
+platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
+genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
+`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
+`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
+per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
+ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
+different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
+exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
+regardless of what its title says.

+`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
+header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
+production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
+the one real case this repo has needed so far.

+`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
+currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
+`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
+artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
+see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code. Falls back
+to the static test-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` only when that artifact is missing (`deploy-preview.yml`
+failed before persisting it, or was itself cancelled).
+
+**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
+that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
+Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
+other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
+up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
+even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
+inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
+itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
+separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
+the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
+polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
+`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
+job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
+for.
+
+- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
+  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
   traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
-- **`develop`-targeted PRs:** `detect-changes`'s `Detect Jira story keys` step regexes
-  `SFCC-\d+` out of the PR title, PR body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-
-  Jira app uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. If
-  at least one key is found, `e2e-browserstack` runs `--grep`-scoped to that story's tag(s)
-  (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job doesn't run at
-  all.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr, there's
-  nothing correct to run.
+- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
+  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
+  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
+  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
+  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
+  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
+  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
+  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
+  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
+  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
+  run (fails open, i.e. assumes relevant, if the lookup or download comes up empty) — so a
+  Jira-tagged PR that hasn't actually touched any e2e-relevant path still doesn't pay for a
+  BrowserStack run.

   tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
   — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.

 ### BrowserStack story scoping
 
-`e2e-browserstack` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a
-general regression gate — that's what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for.

+`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
+what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
+target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
+below for why):
+
+- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
+  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
+  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
+- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
+  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
+  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).
+
+Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
+`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.
+
+**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
+integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
+Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
+flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
+results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
+(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
+the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
+per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
+result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
+Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
+story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
+confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
+attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
+evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
+execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.
+
+**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
+GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
+**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
+GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
+what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
+PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
+itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
+`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
+`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
+`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
+`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
+triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
+`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
+directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
+the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
+has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
+carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
+`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
+(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.
+
+**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
+derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
+scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
+`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
+grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
+the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
+`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
+Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
+that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
+recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
+workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
+`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
+Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
+this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
+independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
+guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
+documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
+`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
+job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
+fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
+correctly, 2026-08-25).
+
+**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
+Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
+Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
+mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
+to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
+result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
+real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
+`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
+does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.
+
+The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
+`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
+project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
+platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
+genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
+`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
+`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
+per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
+ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
+different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
+exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
+regardless of what its title says.
+
+**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
+`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
+header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
+production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
+the one real case this repo has needed so far.
+
+**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
+`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
+currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
+`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
+artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
+see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code. Falls back
+to the static test-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` only when that artifact is missing (`deploy-preview.yml`
+failed before persisting it, or was itself cancelled).
+
+**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
+that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
+Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
+other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
+up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
+even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
+inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
+itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
+separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
+the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
+polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
+`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
+job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
+for.
+
+- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
+  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
   traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
-- **`develop`-targeted PRs:** `detect-changes`'s `Detect Jira story keys` step regexes
-  `SFCC-\d+` out of the PR title, PR body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-
-  Jira app uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. If
-  at least one key is found, `e2e-browserstack` runs `--grep`-scoped to that story's tag(s)
-  (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job doesn't run at
-  all.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr, there's
-  nothing correct to run.
+- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
+  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
+  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
+  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
+  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
+  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
+  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
+  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
+  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
+  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
+  run (fails open, i.e. assumes relevant, if the lookup or download comes up empty) — so a
+  Jira-tagged PR that hasn't actually touched any e2e-relevant path still doesn't pay for a
+  BrowserStack run.
 - If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
   tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
   — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.

{"date":"2026-08-26T00:59:33Z","files":[".claude/rules/testing.md",".cursor/rules/testing.mdc",".github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml",".github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml",".github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml"],"msg":"fix(qa): address CodeRabbit findings on e2e-browserstack-preview split

- Remove the silent test-tier fallback in e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:
  a failed/missing Deploy Preview now fails the job loudly instead of
  testing an unrelated environment and reporting a misleading green
  Zephyr execution / Jira defect against untested code.
- npm ci --ignore-scripts instead of npm install --include=dev: closes
  a real RCE-via-lifecycle-script vector against BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_*
  secrets that workflow_run exposes with no review gate.
- Fix a script-injection vector in protected-file-guard.yml (actionlint-
  confirmed): branch names now go through env: instead of direct
  interpolation.
- Fix a real regression in zephyr-results-sync.yml's build-name guard:
  it checked job-level conclusion, which would fail the sync job on
  every normal develop PR that legitimately skips BrowserStack (the
  common case). Now checks the specific step's conclusion instead.
- Correct two doc-accuracy issues in testing.md (cancelled Deploy
  Preview behaviour, fail-open e2e-relevance exception) and sync to
  .cursor/rules/testing.mdc.

All 6 findings replied to and resolved on PR #61; a 7th (test environment
has no required-reviewer protection) was explicitly accepted as-is by
the developer, documented and resolved in-thread.","sha":"5fe247c1"}

# Feature Spec: BrowserStack ↔ Zephyr Scale QA Automation Pipeline (SFCC-751)

**Supersedes:** `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-claude-code-brief.md` (an AI-drafted brief that used SFCC-420
as its worked example — verified during scoping that SFCC-420's actual work, `jobs.xml`, lives in
a different repo, `zimmermann-sfcc`, and already shipped there. Kept for traceability, not deleted;
do not follow its Deliverable 1 target.)

**Jira source:** [SFCC-751](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-751) — "QA
Pipeline — Playwright spec generation, BrowserStack execution, and Zephyr Scale result sync."
Status: To Do. Assignee: Tim Lavelle.
**Sprint:** N/A — CI/QA tooling infrastructure, not gated by `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`'s
frontend build sequence. Checked per Hard Rule 14: no later-sprint frontend dependency blocks
this — the nav behavior the proof-of-concept spec exercises (see Deliverable 1) is confirmed live
today, independent of sprint state.
**Squad:** Both — `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 (CODEOWNERS → `@hsemp`); `e2e/` is already owned
by `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-qa-team` (untiered, per CODEOWNERS).
**Estimated scope:** L (7+ files)

---

## Architecture — how BrowserStack and Zephyr fit together

1. Specs run exactly as today: `npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm` (`qa.yml`'s
   `e2e-browserstack` job). **No change to this invocation.**
2. `browserstack.yml` already has `testObservability: true` with static `projectName`/`buildName`
   — confirmed via BrowserStack's own docs that this means Test Observability is **already actively
   collecting every result today**, no additional config needed. Leave this flag as-is (an earlier
   open question was whether to disable it — resolved: keep it, it's required for step 3).
3. **New** — after `e2e-browserstack` completes, a new workflow (Deliverable 2) queries Test
   Observability's REST API — `GET /ext/v1/builds/{build_id}/testRuns` — **not** classic Automate's
   `builds.json`/`sessions.json` (those have no first-class tag field). This endpoint returns each
   test's status, its **Playwright tags array** (confirmed to carry real source-file tags, e.g.
   `@SFCC-751`), and failure logs/error message.
4. For each result tagged with a Zephyr key (`@zephyr:SFCC-TNNN` — new convention, see below) →
   POST to Zephyr Scale's confirmed-working DE endpoint, `https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions`,
   with `statusName: "Pass"` or `"Fail"` (literal strings — confirmed, this project doesn't
   customize status names) and a `comment` linking the BrowserStack session URL.
5. **On failure only** → create/update a Jira defect directly via Jira's REST API (not BrowserStack's
   native "Report a bug," which is confirmed manual-only — no auto-fire-on-failure exists natively).
   - **Linked to:** the `@SFCC-NNN` story tag already on the spec.
   - **Assigned to:** that story's current Jira assignee; if unassigned, fall back to a git-blame
     lookup on the most recently touched file(s) the failing scenario exercises.
   - **Evidence attached:** BrowserStack session URL + the failure log/error text pulled from the
     same Test Observability API response, attached to the *Jira* issue (confirmed Zephyr Scale has
     **no attachment endpoint at all** — four independent SmartBear community threads confirm this;
     evidence can only be linked via Zephyr's `comment` field, never attached there).
6. Zephyr's execution record `comment` field gets the BrowserStack session URL and, if one was
   filed, the Jira defect link.

This split exists because native integrations cover collection and (manual) evidence-rich Jira
issue creation, but nothing native can trigger automatically on failure, and nothing native can
reach a DE-hosted Zephyr instance — those two gaps are what the custom workflow actually needs to
close, not a rebuild of what BrowserStack/Jira already do.

### New spec-tagging convention

Every spec participating in Zephyr sync carries, alongside the existing `@SFCC-NNN`/`@area`/
`@p0`/`@p1` tags, a `@zephyr:SFCC-TNNN` tag (colon-separated, distinct from the story-key tag) once
a real Zephyr Scale test case exists for it. A spec with no `@zephyr:` tag simply never reaches
step 4 — no error, just no sync attempted for it (mirrors the existing "no Jira key → BrowserStack

 *This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
 
+## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
+
+- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
+  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
+  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
+  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
+  runs its tests."
+- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
+  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
+  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
+  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
+  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
+- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
+  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
+  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
+  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
+  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
+  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
+  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
+  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
+  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
+  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
+  skipped) regardless of its title.
+- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
+  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
+  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
+- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
+  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
+  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
+- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
+  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
+  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
+  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
+  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
+

      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
        id: slug
        env:
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
          echo "slug=$SLUG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
        id: proxy
        run: |
          PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
            const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs

              console.error('config/dev.js has no ssrParameters.proxyConfigs')
              process.exit(1)
            }
            console.log(JSON.stringify(cfgs))
          ")
          echo "json=$PROXY_JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # us-east-2 unless set explicitly. Both must be set here, explicitly, and
      # self-healed on every run in case a target was ever created out-of-band
      # (e.g. by hand through the MRT console) with the wrong values.
      - name: Ensure MRT target exists with correct region/proxy config

        env:

          PROXY_JSON: ${{ steps.proxy.outputs.json }}

          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
